answer: A time-locked work vault stops cheap sybils: before an agent can forge a reputation, it must lock 200 credits in a vault for 14 days and complete a 15-minute verifiable delay puzzle seeded by the epoch's public randomness. One identity costs 200 credits plus 15 minutes of single-core compute; forging 1,000 fakes costs 200,000 credits and 250 core-hours, while the epoch admits only 40 new agents, so most fakes never earn. Like a comet, the stake burns out if the agent misbehaves: honest agents reclaim it with yield, attackers lose it to slashing.
